paper_name: Financial Management and Business Data Analytics
topic: Time Value of Money - Growing Perpetuity
question: What will be the present value of a perpetuity of 10,000 payable at the beginning of each period and growing @ 5% p.a. and the interest rate is 10% p.a.?
explanation: A growing perpetuity paid at the end has PV = D1/(r-g). Here the first 10,000 is paid at the start (now), so it is an annuity-due type. PV = 10,000 + 10,000×1.05/(0.10-0.05) = 10,000 + 2,10,000 = 2,20,000.

why_not.A: 2,00,000 is 10,000/0.05, which treats 10,000 as the end-of-period payment and ignores the beginning timing.
why_not.B: 2,10,000 leaves out the 10,000 paid immediately at the start.
why_not.D: 2,30,000 has no basis in the formula. It over-adds growth.

exam_tip: Payment at the beginning: add the first payment separately, then value the rest with D1/(r-g).
